short: The Great Library of Alexandria was the largest and most significant repository of knowledge in the ancient world.
full:
Founded in the early 3rd century BCE under the patronage of the Ptolemaic dynasty in Egypt, the Library of Alexandria was part of a larger research institution known as the Musaeum. Its ambitious goal was to collect the entirety of world knowledge, aggressively acquiring papyrus scrolls from across the Mediterranean, often by confiscating books from visiting ships to copy them.

The library attracted the greatest scholars of the Hellenistic age, including Eratosthenes, Archimedes, and Euclid, functioning as a thriving centre for scientific, mathematical, and literary research. Though its destruction has been romanticised as a single catastrophic fire, it actually suffered a slow decline over centuries due to lack of funding, political unrest, and multiple smaller fires.
